title: Tool Endpoints: Validated & Audited
objective: After this lesson you will be able to expose agent tools as HTTP endpoints with schema validation, idempotency keys, approval gates, and audit trails — consumable by any client, not just your UI.
why: Agent tools behind HTTP become products: the React UI calls them, future mobile apps will, and partners might. Endpoint discipline (validation, keys, gates, audit) makes tools safe for unknown callers — the MCP server lessons applied over HTTP with web threat models (retries across networks, auth per call, crawlers hitting GETs).

blocks.text: Endpoints mirror tools, plus web threats

Each agent tool gets an HTTP twin: same schema, same validation, plus **per-call auth** (principal resolved per request), **network retry safety** (idempotency keys required on mutations — retries cross networks constantly), and **rate limits** (per key/tenant). Tool logic shared (same service methods agents call); transport concerns layered at the controller, never inside domain logic.

blocks.caption: Guard order: auth → validate → keys → gates → execute → audit

blocks.text: Validate authentication **first**: validation errors on unauthenticated requests leak schema details to attackers (which fields exist, what formats). 401 before 400, always — error precedence is a security decision. Rate limits sit beside auth (throttle anonymous aggressively, authenticated by tier).

blocks.title: Guard the endpoint
blocks.note: Run it: expect auth, key, gate, key, ok — in order. Approval without a key still fails (keys precede gates); the read tool passes freely.

items: Tool twins: same schemas/validation as agent tools + per-call auth + network-grade idempotency
Guard order auth → validate → keys → gates: precedence is security, oracle prevention first
Reads flow freely; money gated+keyed+audit — endpoint discipline mirrors tool discipline

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice guard chain and map all five verdicts. (b) Explain why case 4 (approval present, key missing) still fails — with the ordering principle. (c) Add a rate-limit check (position it in the chain with reason) plus a test proving anonymous throttling.
hints: Verdicts: auth / key / gate / key-again / ok-read (in order) — keys precede gates, both after auth.
Case 4 fails on keys despite approval: ordering principle (keys before gates) — approval can't bless an unkeyed money call.
Rate limit beside auth (throttle anonymous aggressively): position before validation (cheap reject) with tiered quotas.
exercise.why: Ordering principles (auth→keys→gates), per-case verdicts, and rate-limit placement are the three endpoint judgments — each verified against crafted requests.
exercise.code: // Guard-chain pattern: auth, validate, keys, gates, execute, audit — in that order.

quiz.q: Validation errors returned before auth checks. Issue?
options: Oracle leak: unauthenticated callers learn schema details — 401 before 400, always
quiz.explain: Error precedence is security: authentication gates all detail. Validation-first leaks field shapes to attackers.

quiz.q: Approval present but idempotency key missing on refund call. Verdict?
options: Refuse: keys precede gates — approval blesses keyed calls, never unkeyed ones (recovery would double-charge)
quiz.explain: Ordering principles compose: approval authorizes, keys deduplicate. Unkeyed approval is authorization without safety.

quiz.q: Rate limiting placement in the chain?
options: Beside auth (early, cheap reject) with tiered quotas — throttles anonymous aggressively before spending validation compute
quiz.explain: Early cheap rejects protect compute: throttle before validating, tier by trust, honest statuses for legitimate overflow.

summary: Tool twins with per-call auth, guard order (auth→keys→gates), rate limits beside auth, audit always. Endpoints hold the same discipline as tools, plus web threats.
next: Acting endpoints secured — now remembering across restarts: threads, messages, and checkpoints owned per user. Next: persistence.
